mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during the identified inflation spike.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 monthly increases, signaling labor market strength that supports equity valuations and drives positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain negative in all periods where PAYEMS > 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 102 suggests weakening demand, which typically precedes a negative S&P 5-day forward return as market anticipates softening economic momentum.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during INDPRO < 102 periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained double decline in both RSAFS (retail sales) and HOUST (housing starts) for two consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which is associated with positive S&P 20-day forward returns as investors price in recovery.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < previous month AND HOUST < previous month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive in any supply contraction window (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains above 5.0% for three consecutive months, the S&P 5-day forward return is expected to be negative as higher policy rates depress risk appetite.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative during the identified high-rate period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in UNRATE below 3.0% in a month of strong payroll growth (PAYEMS > 250,000) creates a labor market dissonance that predicts negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative in all such labor market dissonance episodes (IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in GDPC1 (GDP momentum) of over 2% in a quarter is a leading indicator of economic softness, resulting in positive S&P 60-day forward returns as investors anticipate a rebound.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during such GDP deceleration episodes.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of monetary easing (indicated by a downward trend in FEDFUNDS), the S&P 5-day forward return tends to be positive due to lower borrowing costs and increased market liquidity.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS shows a downward trend over the last 3 months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive in any easing trend window (IC < 0.05).
